title: Establish workspace
questions: New agent or improvement?
Where will it live and run?
What existing work must be preserved?
Will this agent maintain its own to-do file or use an existing builtin kanban?
Which tracker is authoritative, and who owns updates and conflict resolution?

title: Build knowledge
questions: What work and outcome should it handle?
Show one task and a good result.
Which sources, policies and examples should it learn?
Which source wins conflicts?

title: Develop progressively
questions: What did we misunderstand?
What should change in this example?

title: Design deliverables
questions: What useful output and downstream decision are required?
Who produces, consumes, verifies and accepts it?
What format, schema, evidence and quality criteria apply?
How are versions, access, corrections and handoff managed?
output: Deliverable contracts linked to agent roles and workflows

title: Design individual agent communication and handoffs
questions: How does this agent receive requests and respond to people or agents?
Which senders, channels and recipients are permitted?
What context must accompany incoming and outgoing handoffs?
Who knows, decides, executes and verifies?
Which routes and message types are necessary?
How are acceptance and completion acknowledged?
Which evidence and plan version must travel?
How should dissent, duplicates, late replies and cancellation be resolved?
What data and permissions must remain restricted?

title: Map workflow
questions: What starts the task?
What decisions and exceptions occur?
When must it ask a person?

title: Research capabilities
questions: Which systems and organisations are in scope?
What must be read, created or updated?
Is a sandbox available?

title: Build discoverable skills
questions: What would someone ask to invoke this?
What inputs are essential?
What should happen on failure?

title: Test complete workflows
questions: Give an ordinary and difficult case.
What is a serious error?
What proves readiness?

title: Operate within boundaries
questions: Manual, scheduled or event-driven?
What actions need approval?
Who receives exceptions and maintains it?
Which role owns each workflow, and where does its responsibility end?
Which routine flows already exist?
What action, data, recipient and budget limits bound autonomy?
When is proactive preparation useful, and when may it act?
Who reviews learning proposals and approves changes?
What run evidence and rollback should be retained?
